Small and mid-sized advisers are generally registered with, and primarily regulated by, one or more state securities authorities.

Large advisers are registered with the SEC and are primarily subject to federal regulation instead of state regulation.
answer: Investment adviser registration generally depends on the adviser’s regulatory assets under management (RAUM). Small advisers have less than $25 million of RAUM, and mid-sized advisers have between $25 million and $100 million; they are generally registered with state securities authorities. Large advisers have more than $100 million of RAUM and are generally registered with the SEC. These are general rules, not absolute ones: the source describes exceptions under which some smaller advisers may register with the SEC.
